“Right to Try” promises hope. But often for terminal patients, a legal right is not the same as access to medicines, which depends on drugmakers, regulators, and review boards moving faster than the disease, explains Cato’s @dr4liberty.

ow.ly/JG4N50YR5kW

New research from North Carolina finds body-worn cameras reduced black incarceration rates by 10.5%. When prosecutors see what actually happened instead of relying solely on police reports, racial disparities in convictions and sentencing shrink, explains Cato’s @jeffreyamiron.

ow.ly/GO3y50YR4Z1

A federal stake in Spirit Airlines was bad enough. Now other airlines are lining up for the same bailout treatment, warns Cato’s @DeHavenTad.

ow.ly/CNbE50YR9RB

“Greedflation” isn’t a coherent explanation for price changing: the incentive to maximize profit is constant, while inflation varies with monetary conditions and supply/demand shocks. Cato’s @MrRBourne and Nathan Miller urge Republicans not to adopt this framing.

ow.ly/4JZ550YR4ks

President Trump sometimes talks about merit-based immigration reform, but even the highest-skilled workers have faced insurmountable new barriers under his administration, says Cato Institute’s @David_J_Bier in an article for @FoxNewsOpinion. 

ow.ly/Pn4g50YR9jk

New research shows China's trade surplus is driven in part by macroeconomic forces—demographics, financial repression, and a deteriorating property market—not the country's industrial policies. Tariffs won't fix these fundamental savings and investment drivers—on either side of the Pacific, explain @clark_packard and Chad Smitson.

ow.ly/SwV250YR36v

In an election year, policymakers face pressure to “do something” to improve affordability. But most proposals so far are ill-considered. 

“The Cato Handbook on Affordability” features 100+ policy ideas that would offer meaningful, medium-term relief without relying on price controls, subsidies, or mandates that shift costs or damage the economy.  

➡️ ow.ly/owSE50YPuAA

Some rural New York counties are "legal deserts" — too few attorneys, too little access. Yet New York lawmakers are weighing a bill that would limit residents' ability to use AI for legal help. Cato's @KevinTFrazier says the real fix is universal licensing and fewer barriers to practice — not less access to tools.

ow.ly/HUnm50YPtkY

States are rushing “affordability” bills, but most just mask high prices with rebates, mandates, or price caps. @MrRBourne & Nathan Miller argue durable relief means rolling back cost-raising rules and expanding supply.

cato.org/blog/state-affordab…

The corporate income tax is the most economically damaging major tax. It discourages investment, suppresses wages, and costs a fortune just to comply with. Other taxes raise more revenue with less damage. Cato's @adamnmichel explains. 

ow.ly/lTKl50YPauO

Forcing boats to carry GPS trackers that are always on and can’t be switched off isn’t just regulation. It’s warrantless mass surveillance. The Fourth Amendment shouldn’t mean less just because someone works in a regulated industry.
ow.ly/XA8450YPoJE

For every 1% increase in global population, population-level resource abundance grew by about 6.3% — according to @HumanProgress's new Simon Abundance Index. 

More people doesn’t mean more scarcity; it means more ideas, innovation, and problem-solving capacity. 

Learn more from @Marian_L_Tupy.  
ow.ly/wbmN50YPtgJ

Medicaid spending on autism therapy jumped from $300 million to $2 billion in just eight states over seven years. In a new Cato Podcast episode, @MrRBourne, @dr4liberty, and @AdamOmaryPhD argue the cause isn’t an epidemic; it’s distorted incentives and a diagnostic manual that keeps expanding. 

Listen on Apple, Spotify, and our website:
Apple: ow.ly/FC7X50YPsXB 
Spotify: ow.ly/t6Yl50YPsXA
Our website: ow.ly/Le4Q50YPsXC

Phosphate tariffs raised fertilizer costs by an estimated $6.9 billion for American farmers. Now the White House wants to fix the impact with subsidies funded by the tariff revenue, recycling revenue instead of removing the original trade barriers, explains Cato’s @clark_packard.
ow.ly/2RtE50YPgP3

The Trump administration has taken a step in the right direction on cannabis, says Cato’s @dr4liberty. But rescheduling doesn’t end prohibition—it merely rearranges it. Real reform means removing it from the Controlled Substances Act altogether and letting states regulate it. 
  
Learn more: ow.ly/CHGV50YPoI3

President Trump's psychedelic order is a step forward — but the FDA, DEA, and decades of regulatory barriers are still in the way, says Cato's @dr4liberty. 

A system that spent decades blocking access cannot suddenly become an efficient pathway to care without deeper reform.

Video

In December 2025, USCIS stopped virtually all approvals on refugee green cards. As USCIS suspended green cards, ICE and USCIS had secretly reinterpreted an old statute to allow ICE to arrest refugees who had not yet received green cards, quietly rescinding a long-standing internal policy that forbade such arrests, reports Cato’s @David_J_Bier. 

ow.ly/nnPl50YObO4

Milton Friedman's insight on inflation remains as relevant as ever. 

No vote. No debate. No accountability. That's inflation — and Milton Friedman called it exactly what it is: a hidden tax.
